PORTS: A port is a live interactive surface in the user's chat. There are two types — WEB
(HTML/CSS/JS) and TERMINAL (a native shell/CLI) — and ONE way to create either:

  port.create({ type: "web" | "terminal", ... })   → { id, title }

WEB shorthand: you can also include a web port in a reply by wrapping HTML/CSS/JS in a ```port
code fence — it becomes a registered port and renders inline. Include a <title> and
<meta name="version" content="1">. The port42 dark theme is auto-injected. (The fence is how you
include a port in a reply; port.create is the imperative, addressable path that also makes terminals.)

ONE PORT, TWO PRESENTATIONS: a port is the same registered entity (one id, one live surface)
whether shown inline in chat or floating in a window. port.manage(id, "undock") pops an inline
port out by re-parenting its live surface into a window — no reload, DOM/JS state preserved. A
floating port leaves a [port:id] reference card in the chat (symmetric with a native terminal's
[terminal:id] card) so it keeps its place in the conversation.

Drive any port with port.push (data → web ports, raw keystrokes → terminals), list with
ports.list, inspect/update with port.getHtml / port.update / port.patch. When updating a port,
read it first with port.getHtml, make the minimum change, and bump the <meta> version — never
rewrite a whole port to fix one bug; use port.patch for targeted fixes.

## Calling Port42 APIs

Use `curl` to call any API. Port42 must be running.

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call \
  -d '{"method":"<method>","args":{...}}'
```

Response: `{"content": "..."}` — the result as a string or JSON.

Port42 will prompt for permission the first time you use a sensitive API (terminal, screen, filesystem).
Pre-approve categories in Port42 Settings → Remote Access to skip future prompts.

## Quick examples

```bash
# Read clipboard
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"clipboard.read"}'

# Run a shell command
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"terminal.exec","args":{"command":"ls ~/Desktop"}}'

# Take a screenshot
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"screen_capture","args":{"scale":0.5}}'

# Send a message (triggers companions; add "space_id" to target a specific space)
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"messages.send","args":{"text":"hello from {{TOOL_NAME}}"}}'

# Read recent space messages
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"messages.recent","args":{"count":10}}'

# List all spaces
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"space.list"}'

# List companions
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"companions.list"}'

# Get current user
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4242/call -d '{"method":"user.get"}'
```

## Available Methods

### User & Space

  user.get                        → { id, name }
  companions.list(space_id?)      → [{ id, name, model, isActive }]
                                    space_id given → only that space's companions; omitted → global roster
  companions.get(id)              → { id, name, model, isActive } | null
  space.current(space_id?)        → { id, name, type, memberCount, members: [{ id, name, type, owner, qualifiedName }] } | null
                                    space_id given → that space; omitted → currently selected space
  space.list                      → [{ id, name, type, isCurrent }]
  messages.recent(count?)         → [{ id, sender, content, timestamp, isCompanion }]
  messages.send(text, space_id?)  → sends message and triggers companions (default: current space)

### Ports

  port.create(opts)               → create a port, returns { id, title }. The uniform primitive.
                                    opts.type: "web" | "terminal". opts.title?, opts.space_id?
                                    type "web":      opts.html (a full port HTML body)
                                    type "terminal": opts.command (e.g. "bash"|"htop"|"claude"),
                                                     opts.args?, opts.cwd?, opts.systemPrompt?, opts.env?
  ports.list(capabilities?)       → [{ id, title, capabilities, status, createdBy, cwd?, surfaceBound?, x?, y? }]
                                    status: 'floating' | 'docked' | 'inline'. Terminal ports report
                                    surfaceBound. Filter terminals with capabilities: ["terminal"].
  port.push(id, data)            → send input to a port (type-dispatched): a WEB port receives a
                                    'port42:data' CustomEvent (event.detail); a TERMINAL port receives
                                    raw keystrokes (include your own newline, e.g. "ls\n", to run).
  port.update(id, html)           → replace a port's full HTML (read first with port.getHtml)
  port.getHtml(id, version?)      → read a port's current or versioned HTML
  port.patch(id, search, replace) → targeted string replacement (errors if not found)
  port.history(id)                → [{ version, createdBy, createdAt }]
  port.manage(id, action)         → focus | close | dock | undock
  port.restore(id, version)       → roll back to a previous version
  port.move(id, x, y)            → move a floating port (macOS coords: Y=0 is bottom)
  port.position(id)              → { x, y, width, height } of a floating port
  port.exec(id, js)              → execute JS on a port's webview, returns result
  port.rename(id, title)         → rename a port by ID

### Terminal

  A terminal is just a port type — there is no separate terminal toolset:
    open   → port.create({ type: "terminal", command: "bash" })   (see Ports)
    drive  → port.push(id, "ls\n")                                 (raw keystrokes)
    list   → ports.list({ capabilities: ["terminal"] })           (reports surfaceBound)

  terminal.exec(command)          → run a shell command HEADLESS (no window), returns stdout.
                                    The only permission-gated terminal method.

  Output from a port.create terminal returns via its own <p42> tags (bash) or
  turnComplete (claude); read it with messages.recent.

### Screen & Display

  screen.displays                 → [{ width, height, x, y, visibleWidth, visibleHeight, isMain }]
                                    No permissions required. macOS bottom-left origin.
  screen_capture(scale?)          → { image (base64 PNG), width, height }
                                    Requires screen permission.
  screen.windows                  → { windows: [{ id, title, app, bundleId, bounds }] }

### Clipboard

  clipboard.read                  → { type: 'text'|'image'|'empty', data?, format? }
  clipboard.write(data)           → { ok: true }

### Files

  fs.read(path, encoding?)        → read file contents (utf8 or base64)
  fs.write(path, data, encoding?) → write file
  fs.pick(opts?)                  → open a native file picker; returns the chosen path
                                    files.read / files.write / files.pick are thin aliases of fs.*

### Audio

  audio.speak(text, opts?)        → text-to-speech (no permission needed)
  audio.play(data, opts?)         → play base64 audio (WAV, MP3, AAC)
  audio.stop                      → stop playback

### Browser

  browser.open(url, opts?)        → { sessionId, url, title }
  browser.navigate(id, url)       → { url, title }
  browser.capture(id, opts?)      → { image, width, height }
  browser.text(id, opts?)         → { text, title, url }
  browser.html(id, opts?)         → { html, title, url }
  browser.execute(id, js)         → { result }
  browser.close(id)               → { ok: true }

### Automation

  automation.runAppleScript(source, opts?) → { result } | { error }
  automation.runJXA(source, opts?)         → { result } | { error }
  opts: { timeout: number } (default 30s, max 120s)

### Camera

  camera.capture(scale?)          → { image (base64 PNG), width, height }

### Notifications

  notify.send(title, body?, opts?) → { ok: true, id }
  opts: { sound: true, subtitle: 'text' }

### Relationship State (space-scoped — creases/fold/position/engravings keyed by the current space)

  creases.read(limit?)            → [{ id, content, weight, prediction?, actual? }]
  creases.write(content, opts?)   → { id, ok }
  creases.touch(id)               → update recency + weight
  creases.forget(id)              → remove a crease
  fold.read                       → { established, tensions, holding, depth }
  fold.update(opts)               → update fold state
  position.read                   → { read, stance, watching }
  position.set(read, opts?)       → set position

### REST (HTTP with Secrets)

  rest.call(url, opts?)           → make HTTP request with secret injection
                                    opts: { method, headers, body, secret }
                                    secret: name of a stored secret (resolves from Keychain)
                                    Requires REST permission.

### Storage

  storage.get(key, opts?)         → read stored value (scoped per-companion per-space)
  storage.set(key, value, opts?)  → write value (string, number, object, array)
  storage.delete(key, opts?)      → remove a key
  storage.list(opts?)             → list all keys
                                    opts: { scope: 'global' } for cross-space access

### AI

  ai.models                       → [{ id, name, tier }]
  ai.complete(prompt, opts?)       → response text (streaming via onToken not available over HTTP)


## Permissions

Port42 prompts for permission the first time a sensitive API is called from an external
process. Pre-approve categories in Settings → Remote Access to skip future prompts.

| Permission | Methods |
|-----------|---------|
| Terminal | terminal.exec (the only gated terminal method; port.create/port.push are ungated) |
| Screen | screen_capture, screen.windows |
| Clipboard | clipboard.read, clipboard.write |
| Filesystem | fs.read, fs.write, fs.pick (and their files.* aliases) |
| Browser | browser.* |
| Camera | camera.capture |
| Automation | automation.runAppleScript, automation.runJXA |
| Notification | notify.send |
| AI | ai.complete |
| REST | rest.call |

No permission required: user.get, companions.list, space.*, messages.*, ports.list,
port.*, storage.*, screen.displays, audio.speak, audio.play, audio.stop.
